brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: edit.duplicate
objective.description: Duplicate one or more local Brique elements into new local targets.

#root.role: Validate one duplication batch, copy the targeted local elements to new local names, and return one aggregated per-item result payload.

items._comment: Required non-empty duplication batch. Each item: { type (string: context|capacity|schema|document), source_name (string), target_name (string), destination_ctx_id (optional string — absolute context path, defaults to addressed context) }.

result._comment: Per-item result list. Each item: { ok (bool), type (string), source_name (string), target_name (string) } on success, or { ok: false, ..., error: { code, message, reason } } on failure.

effects.context_tree: Local files, directories, and meaning descriptors may be copied under new local names.

transformation_contract.morphing: A batch of local duplication requests becomes a per-item duplication result set, with successful items producing new local copies of the requested Brique elements.
invariants: edit.duplicate is batch-oriented and returns one result entry per parsed item.
Duplication is a pure copy primitive in v1 and refuses any patch payload in the same item.
Context duplication copies the whole child context tree while filtering out .git paths.
Descriptor duplication preserves source key order; target-local document adjustments retain existing key positions and append only missing keys.
When duplicating within the same context (no destination_ctx_id, or destination_ctx_id equal to the addressed context), source_name and target_name must differ.
When duplicating to a different context, source_name and target_name may be identical, since the destination context is a distinct namespace.
success: On success, each result item reports ok=true with the normalized type plus source_name and target_name.
Document duplication preserves local content semantics by copying the local file and rewriting brique.file deterministically for the target name.
failure: The capacity fails when params.items is missing or cannot be parsed into a valid edit batch.

Individual items return errors when the type is unsupported, names are missing, source_name and target_name are equal within the same context, destination_ctx_id cannot be resolved, the source cannot be read, the target already exists, or copying cannot complete.
notes: Matter and structure duplication is refused here because those element kinds are owned by MatterLoop.
Duplicate does not mutate the copied meaning beyond the target-local adjustments needed for documents and contexts.
